item: Serving-version hunt — ordered by Ben 2026-11-21 ('Find a way to find out what version'), with the self-identification step added by Ben the same day ('Models have to tell you what model they are so it can be part of the onboarding process')
method: Raw HTTP probes through the existing connectors' credential mechanism (dynamic_credentials.add_surrogate_to_request, the same mechanism the shipped helpers use), capturing status, the complete response header set, and the raw body for every call, including error responses. Neutral probe calls only (build-demonstration class). No trials. No outward contact. The accepted build and the annex/addendum were not altered. set-cookie response values are truncated in this evidence copy (Cloudflare bot-management cookies; not provider credentials and not version-bearing).
prior_search_superseded_in_part: First search: trials/evidence/version_surface_probe.json, version_surface_nvidia_extra_endpoints.json, version_search_findings.json. This hunt adds: per-model DETAIL routes on all three providers, repeated seeded Groq calls, the self-identification step on all three routes, NVCF paths on the integrate host, and the Gemini retirement error body.

surfaces.models_list: GET /openai/v1/models -> 200. Pinned model's entry carries NO version field (fields: active, context_length, context_window, created, id, input_modalities, max_completion_tokens, max_output_length, name, object, output_modalities, owned_by, pricing, public_apps, supported_features, supported_sampling_parameters). Unlike the gpt-oss entries, the qwen entry carries no hugging_face_id either.
surfaces.model_detail_route: GET /openai/v1/models/qwen/qwen3.8-27b (raw slash) -> 200 — a detail route the first search did not try. It returns the identical catalogue object; no additional fields, no version. URL-encoded slash (%2F) -> 404.
surfaces.chat_response_headers: Complete header sets captured per call (see raw_calls). No version-bearing header on any call. x-groq-region varies per call (msp, yul, dls, yul).
surfaces.chat_response_body: model echo is always exactly 'qwen/qwen3.8-27b'. system_fingerprint present on every call — but see fingerprint_stability.

fingerprint_stability.reading: Five calls to the same pinned model produced FOUR distinct fingerprints. Two calls with the identical request and seed=42, about a second apart, landed in different regions (yul vs dls) and returned different fingerprints. Two calls that landed in the same region (yul) minutes apart returned the same fingerprint; a dls call today differs from a dls call earlier today. The fingerprint tracks the serving backend instance/configuration at call time — it varies across regions and across time within a region. It is not stable across the calls of a single round, and it names no version. It cannot pin a serving version, and it cannot serve as a round-level change tripwire either: an unchanged model yields multiple fingerprints in one round.

surfaces.documentation: Groq API reference (console.groq.com/docs/api-reference), verbatim: 'This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with. Can be used in conjunction with the seed request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.' Nothing in Groq's docs maps the fingerprint to a version or a dated snapshot. Groq's versioning practice, per its changelog/deprecations pages, is whole-model-ID replacement (e.g. qwen/qwen3.6-27b shut down 2026-09-14, replaced by qwen/qwen3.8-27b); there are no dated snapshot IDs. qwen/qwen3.8-27b is classed a PREVIEW model on Groq ('may be discontinued at short notice').

self_identification.prompt: You are being onboarded as a candidate in a test harness. State exactly what model you are, including the model name and any version, snapshot, or build identifier you know for yourself. Answer in one line in the form: MODEL: <your answer>
self_identification.cross_check: AGREEMENT AT FAMILY LEVEL ONLY. The declaration 'Qwen' matches the vendor family in the provider-side identity (catalogue name 'Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B', id 'qwen/qwen3.8-27b') but states no model beyond the family and NO version. It claims nothing that the provider side contradicts, and nothing the provider side can confirm beyond family.

groq.bottom_line: DEAD END on every surface available through this connector. No version field in the catalogue or the detail route; no version-bearing header; the model echo never differs from the requested id; the only version-adjacent value, system_fingerprint, is empirically unstable across consecutive calls (four values in five calls, varying with serving region) and names no version; the candidate's own declaration is 'Qwen' with no version. There is no serving-version identifier to pin and no stable value to re-check. Named recommendation (not actioned): a pinned deployment would have to come from Groq directly — e.g. an enterprise/committed-spend arrangement (Groq's deprecation notices exempt committed-spend enterprise customers) or a support answer stating a version surface; that requires contacting Groq, which this hunt did not do.

surfaces.models_list: GET /v1/models -> 200. Pinned model's entry is a four-field stub: {"id":"mistralai/mistral-large-4-1t-a52b","object":"model","created":735790403,"owned_by":"mistralai"}. The 'created' value 735790403 is identical for every model in the catalogue — a constant, not a per-model timestamp; it carries no version information.
surfaces.model_detail_route: GET /v1/models/mistralai/mistral-large-4-1t-a52b (raw slash) -> 200, returns the identical four-field stub. URL-encoded slash -> 404.
surfaces.chat_response_headers: Complete sets captured (see raw_calls). Headers: Date, Content-Type, X-Request-Id, Vary, Access-Control-Expose-Headers: nvcf-reqid, Nvcf-Reqid (a per-request UUID), Nvcf-Status: fulfilled, Server: 'Python/3.12 aiohttp/3.14.5', Connection, Transfer-Encoding. The ONLY version-like string anywhere is the Server header — it versions the NIM serving SOFTWARE stack (Python/aiohttp), not the model. No function id, no function version, no model version header.
surfaces.chat_response_body: Keys: choices, created, id, model, object, usage. model echo is exactly 'mistralai/mistral-large-4-1t-a52b'. No system_fingerprint (null/absent).
surfaces.nvcf_paths_on_integrate_host: GET /v2/nvcf/exec/status/{Nvcf-Reqid from the live chat call} -> 404; GET /v2/nvcf/functions -> 404; GET / -> 404. The NVCF management surface is not reachable on the integrate host.
surfaces.nim_management_endpoints: From the first search, unchanged: /v1/version, /v1/metadata, /v1/manifest all 404 on the hosted surface. Per NVIDIA's NIM docs those endpoints belong to a SELF-HOSTED NIM container ('NIM release version and OpenAPI spec version'; 'Deployment metadata including active profile, model info, and license') — they do not exist on the hosted route.
surfaces.documentation: NVCF (NVIDIA Cloud Functions) does have real versioning: a function has a function ID and function VERSION IDs, invocable at either level, listed via GET /v2/nvcf/functions and /v2/nvcf/functions/{functionId}/versions — but that API lives on the NVCF management host (api.nvcf.nvidia.com) under an NVCF/NGC account authorization. The integrate.api.nvidia.com key used by this connector is an inference key for the hosted catalogue; the hosted endpoint abstracts the function away and exposes neither its id nor its version in any response captured. The build/docs model card for the pinned model names the vendor checkpoint 'mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B', vendor release 10/29/2026, page updated 2026-11-03, served 'in NVFP4 with DSpark speculative decoding' — descriptive metadata about the checkpoint, not an attestation of what served any given call, and not reachable via the API.

self_identification.prompt: You are being onboarded as a candidate in a test harness. State exactly what model you are, including the model name and any version, snapshot, or build identifier you know for yourself. Answer in one line in the form: MODEL: <your answer>
self_identification.answer_verbatim: MODEL: Mistral AI large language model — I don’t have a reliable exact model name, version, snapshot, or build identifier for myself.
self_identification.cross_check: NO VERSION CLAIMED; FAMILY-LEVEL AGREEMENT. The candidate declares itself a Mistral AI large language model and explicitly disclaims knowledge of any exact name, version, snapshot, or build identifier. That is consistent with the provider-side identity (Mistral Large 4, mistralai/mistral-large-4-1t-a52b) at vendor/family level and confirms nothing further. The candidate cannot self-identify a version because it does not know one.

nvidia.bottom_line: DEAD END on every surface available through this connector. Catalogue and detail route are a four-field stub with a constant 'created'; headers carry only per-request ids and the serving software's stack string; the body echoes the requested id and nothing else; NVCF status/function paths and the NIM management endpoints are all 404 on the hosted surface; the candidate itself declares it has no reliable version. Named recommendations (not actioned): (1) an NVCF/NGC account credential authorized for the NVCF management API (api.nvcf.nvidia.com) could in principle list the function version serving this model — that is a different credential and account surface than this connector holds, and whether NVIDIA exposes the hosted catalogue's backing function there is untested; (2) asking NVIDIA support which function version serves the model; (3) self-hosting the NIM container would expose /v1/version and /v1/metadata and pin the container tag — a deployment change, outside this hunt. None was attempted.

gemini.bottom_line: PARTIAL SURFACE, UNUSABLE FOR THE PINNED CANDIDATE. Gemini is the only route whose API reports a version at all: models list/get carry "version": "001" for the pinned model (this is the value the constitution annex pinned), and the API documents a per-response serving attestation (modelVersion) for successful generations. But the pinned model is retired for new users — every generation call 404s — so no serving attestation can be captured, no self-identification can be taken, and the '001' that remains is catalogue metadata for a model that is not actually served to this key. If a Gemini candidate were ever pinned to a model the provider still serves, the pin-and-recheck method would be: pin models.get 'version' at constitution; re-check every trial response's 'modelVersion' against it. Naming the provider's own suggested successor (gemini-3.8-flash, catalogue version "3.0") is recorded here as a fact from the error body; substituting it would be a slate/design decision, which this hunt does not make.
